messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: Comparing models 2pl and gpcm
parts:
Hello Phil,

I saw previous threads regarding anova() and negative X2 values; but I thought my doubt is little different as the data in the two comparison models are different.

As 2pl model is a special case of gpcm,  I assumed that one is nested of another and carried out following analysis.

These two data are not that different.

Previously the data were scored polytomously, like 0 - for incorrect, 1- for partially incorrect and 2- for correct.

Later same data was scored as dichotomous by encoding 0 and 1 as 0 and 2 as 1. 

anova(mod_2pl,mod_gpcm)

 

Model 1: mirt(data = dichData, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL", SE = TRUE,TOL = 3 * 1e-04)

Model 2: mirt(data = polyData, model = 1, itemtype = "gpcm", TOL = tol)

 

      AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik        X2  df   p

1 423426.3 423515.8 427149.9 429774.9 -210887.1       NaN NaN NaN

2 512008.4 512144.1 516566.0 519778.8 -254993.2 -88212.08 185   1




Turns out that X2 is negative, which made me think, is this the right way to decide which model should I use? Can I use anova() here?


If not, is there any other way to compare gpcm and 2pl model fit?



P.S. I doubt that how valid this anova() test will be when I am changing the data for two different models, but I thought one data is derived from another, so it might make it comparable.




Thanking you,


Irsahd

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Comparing models 2pl and gpcm
parts:
These models are not nested in any sense of the word. The datasets are entirely different, and therefore comparing AIC or other likelihood based statistics is not appropriate. 

At best, you could try to justify the collapsing via goodness of fit measures from itemfit() or M2(), which don't require nesting, but the comparisons are really more 'expert judgement' than anything really statistical. Cheers.

Phil
